State-Space Models

A state-space model separates the hidden system from the noisy measurements of that system. This separation is the conceptual home of the Kalman Filter.

Two equations

The first equation describes how the hidden state evolves. The second describes how observations are generated from the hidden state.
x_t = A x_{t-1} + B u_t + w_t

The state x_t is hidden. The observation z_t is visible. The matrix A governs evolution, while H maps the hidden state into observed data.

  • w_t is process noise with covariance Q.
  • v_t is measurement noise with covariance R.

Example: position and velocity

Suppose the hidden state contains position and velocity, but the sensor only observes position.
The observation matrix H selects position from the state vector. Velocity is not directly observed, but it can still be inferred because it affects future positions.

blocks.question: What does the observation matrix H do?
options: Maps hidden state into observed measurement space
blocks.explanation: H tells the model which part or combination of the hidden state is observed.
